published_statement: p.4: 'An accurate analytic approximation to the exact numerically calculated scalar field stress energy tensor was developed in Ref. [18] [AHS] ... <T^nu_mu>_analytic = (T)_0 + (xi - 1/6)(T)_1 + (xi - 1/6)^2 (T)_2 + (T)_log (4) ... we find that the semiclassical Einstein equations for a conformally coupled scalar (xi = 1/6) are as follows (K^2 = 1/(5760 pi))': eqs. (5) tt, (6) ll, (7) thth, each LHS = G^mu_nu of metric (2), RHS = K^2[non-log bracket + ln f (log bracket)] (p.5; the text layer reads '+16 f'^2 f''/f^3' in the tt log bracket and '-4 f'^2 r'^2/(f^2 r)' in the ll log bracket). p.6: the ll equation 'is actually a constraint'; throat conditions r(0) > 0, r'(0) = 0, r''(0) >= 0, f(0) > 0, r'(0) = 0 -> f'(0) = 0, f''(0) >= 0, optional reflection symmetry r'''(0) = f'''(0) = 0; 'writing out the ll-equation (6) at the point l = 0 ... yields an algebraic quartic equation for the throat radius r(0)': -4 (f''(0)/f(0))^2 [1 + ln f(0)] r(0)^4 + 32 (f''(0) r''(0)/f(0)) [1 + (1/2) ln f(0)] r(0)^3 + [K^-2 - 16 r''(0)^2 ln f(0)] r(0)^2 + 16 ln f(0) = 0 (8), 'where we have used only that r'(0) = f'(0) = 0 ... independent of the values assigned to the third derivatives'. p.7: 'taking f(0) = f''(0) = 1, r''(0) = 0 and xi = 1/6 yields r(0) ~ 67 l_P'; boundary data (9): '-1 <= ln f(0) < 0; f'(0) = 0; f''(0) = 0; f'''(0) = 0; r(0) = sqrt(-16 K^2 ln f(0)); r'(0) = 0; r''(0) = 0; r'''(0) = 0'; 'a particular numerical solution for ln f(0) = -2/3'; throat 'of radius r(0) ~ 0.02 l_P'. Footnote [20]: 'We have also set the scalar mass and temperature to zero: m = kappa = 0. In this case, the arbitrary renormalization scale parameter mu appearing in (T)_log can be absorbed into the definition of f.'
published_hypotheses: H1 static spherically symmetric metric in proper-distance gauge, ds^2 = -f(l)dt^2 + dl^2 + r^2(l) dOmega^2 (eq. (2), p.4); f(0) > 0 (p.6).
H2 semiclassical Einstein equation G_mu^nu = 8 pi <T_mu^nu> (eqs. (1), (3)), hbar = c = G = 1, MTW signs (footnote [19]).

H3 <T> is NOT the exact expectation value: it is the Anderson-Hiscock-Samuel analytic approximation, eq. (4), described as 'accurate' (p.4); (T)_log 'left in terms of combinations of curvature tensors' by AHS and worked out by HPS (p.4).
H4 a single conformally coupled scalar, xi = 1/6 (p.3, p.4), massless and at zero temperature, m = kappa = 0 (footnote [20]).
H5 the arbitrary renormalization scale mu of (T)_log is 'absorbed into the definition of f' (footnote [20]) -- so the normalization of f, and hence the value ln f(0), carries mu.
H6 throat data: r(0) > 0, r'(0) = 0 (hence f'(0) = 0 by footnote [22]), r''(0) >= 0, f''(0) >= 0; eq. (8) uses only r'(0) = f'(0) = 0 (p.6).
H7 eq. (9) data: -1 <= ln f(0) < 0, all first-to-third derivatives of f and r zero at l = 0, r(0) from (8); the plotted solution has ln f(0) = -2/3 (p.7).
H8 the full xi-dependent equations are 'too lengthy to be shown' (p.5): only xi = 1/6 is printed.

lacked_data: What HPS lacked in 1996-97, and whether it changes their conclusion as the tree uses it. (i) An exact <T_ab> on these metrics: they lacked it, and so does everyone now -- the tree says 'no exact <T_ab> is known on these metrics' (hpscentre.py:36-38); HPS state their source is the AHS analytic approximation (p.3-4), so the conclusion 'a solution of HPS's model system' is not undercut by that absence, while 'a solution of semiclassical gravity' was never established by HPS and is not claimed by the tree. (ii) Exact numerics against which to test the approximation off Schwarzschild/RN-type backgrounds: AHL (1995) already showed a horizon failure; HPS's plotted branch has no horizon. No new datum here moves the HPS-system statements. (iii) A conservation check of their printed equations: the text layer carries two terms (M1, M2) that break nabla_mu T^mu_nu = 0; the unique conserved repair (C4) is also exactly the Bach tensor (C10). Both vanish at the throat (C4f), and the throat numbers (eq. (8), eq. (9), r_0 ~ 0.02 and ~ 67 l_P, the fourth derivatives, rho, p_l, p_t) come out identical in either reading (C6c, C8b). Off the throat the reading matters -- which system HPS actually integrated is NOT DETERMINED in the tree (hpscentre.py HPS_INTEGRATED_THE_PRINTED_SYSTEM) and is a separate entry. (iv) A measured renormalization scale mu: absent then and now; the tree's quoted values are functions of HPS's normalization of f. (v) Measured constants: none enter; Planck-unit results are dimensionless, and l_P (CODATA 2018 1.616255e-35 m) moves nothing. Evidence either way, then: the lacked data (exact <T>, validity of AHS at sub-Planck scales, mu) limit what the HPS solution MEANS physically, which the tree already names (DOMAIN_WORD, sub-Planck as measurement, not-exact <T>); they do not change any equation or number the tree takes from HPS. M's hypothesis is not supported for this result at the level of its mathematics; it is supported in the weaker sense that the printed text carries two internally inconsistent coefficients that only a conservation check reveals.
grade_evidence: The result as the tree uses it -- HPS's model system (5)-(7) at xi = 1/6, m = kappa = 0, in the conserved reading, with eq. (8) and eq. (9) and the numbers derived from them -- is re-derived here from the source text layer, independently of the tree's transcription, and agrees in every checked item (rederive/gr-qc_9701064.py C1-C9 and _bach.py C10, ALL PASS): the Einstein sides, a character-level match of the tree's transcription to the text layer, the uniqueness of the conserving repair (116, 21, r^2), its identity with 24 x Bach, the trace-anomaly form with c = 1, eq. (8) from eq. (6), eq. (9)'s r(0), r_0 = 0.024279 and 67.2599 l_P, f''''/f and r''''/r, rho = -45/L, p_l = -rho, p_t = 0, rho + p_l = -28350 pi l^2, m = r0/2 + O(l^4). The source's two printed coefficients (M1, M2) are DISCREPANCIES of the text layer (journal not read), not refutations; the tree already names them and runs the unique conserved reading, and they vanish at the throat so every throat number is reading-independent. No datum has moved. 'agrees_with_source: partly' records exactly those two text-layer coefficients. Caveats that keep this from being more than STANDS-as-used: (a) the canonical entry omits H5 (mu absorbed into f, footnote [20]) from its hypothesis lists though the code carries it -- the tree's L-dependent numbers are HPS-normalization values, not mu-free; (b) the equality of (5)-(7) with AHS rests on HPS and on Popov's second printing (tree-READ), AHS itself NAMED-NOT-READ -- internal consistency (C4, C5, C10) does not fix a conserved traceless Killing-dependent addition; (c) throatmass.py's 'eq. (8) as transcribed, not re-read' caveat is discharged by C6. The far-zone law (a, b) and 'which system HPS integrated' are separate entries and are not graded here.
what_would_change_the_grade: To NARROWED: a reading of AHS PRD 51 4337 (or its xi = 1/6 restatement) showing HPS's non-log brackets differ from AHS by a conserved traceless tensor (which C4/C5/C10 cannot detect), or the tree quoting r_0 or rho = -45/L as mu-free physical values. To a discrepancy-free STANDS (agrees_with_source: yes): the PRL journal text showing 116 and r^2 as typeset (the defects then belong to the arXiv text layer only). To WRONG: none foreseeable for the tree's use -- the throat quantities are reading-independent and closed-form. Off the throat, whether HPS's published figures belong to the conserved system is OPEN and belongs to the ab-fit / integration entries.
